R0206.title: IoT Hardware Supply Chain Attack
R0206.definition: Attackers implant backdoors in IoT device chips, firmware, communication modules and other hardware supply chain components for long-term persistence and remote control.

references.title: 2024 Cybersecurity Deep Insight: Hardware Supply Chain Risk

R0206.description:
IoT hardware supply chain attacks occur across chips, modules, sensors, firmware, manufacturing, and logistics. Attackers may implant backdoors, replace components, or alter default settings so deployed devices remain controllable.

IoT fleets are large, long-lived, and hard to patch in the field. Supplier verification, firmware signing, hardware sampling, and runtime anomaly monitoring are essential.

Limitation: Requires supply chain penetration capability
R0206.influence: Hardware supply chain compromise can place persistent backdoors into large IoT fleets that are expensive to detect, patch, or recall.

observables: Batch IoT device firmware hashes mismatch the official signed version
Device factory-default configs or firmware contain unexpected remote management channels
Device communication modules show anomalous outbound connections matching known backdoor signatures
New-batch devices exhibit uniform anomalous behavior shortly after deployment
Vendor-delivered components or firmware contain undeclared functions or debug interfaces
